newsitem.title: UK: Hanson dips on profit taking after results.
newsitem.headline: Hanson dips on profit taking after results.

text.p: Shares in British rump building materials group Hanson Plc fell slightly on Thursday as traders decided to take profits after first half earnings failed to excite.
By 1330 GMT the stock fell 7-1/2p to 321p.
The results failed to top market expectations and one analyst commented that he saw nothing to prompt a change in profit forecasts.
"Hanson always tries to sound optimistic, but the market never believes them," a dealer added.

Pro-forma, half-year, pre-tax profits were 47.8 million stg, which was derived after the company took a charge of 49 million stg, which included a 28 million book loss on the sale of Hanson Electrical.
The company said pro-forma operating profits rose nine percent to 121 million pounds.
"It is profit taking, they have had a great run," said one marketmaker.
The stock rallied to a three-month peak of 334p on Monday from a low on July 16 of 280p. It had been hovering around the 330p area ahead of the results.
Hanson said it saw most of its expansion opportunities over the next 12 months coming out of U.S. markets, which are expected to remain buoyant.

The group remained optimistic for the second half of the year, despite a flattening out of first-half growth in some British divisions which it blamed on poor weather in June and the quiet holiday period.
Talks on the sale of Hanson's U.S. hydraulic equipment division Grove Worldwide were ongoing but nothing was imminent, it said.
